@Chris__Iverson @heynavtoor The post accurately summarizes the Sept 2025 OpenAI paper "Why Language Models Hallucinate" (Kalai et al.), including its core math on inevitable errors even with perfect data/unlimited compute, training incentives for guessing, and benchmark scoring that treats "I don't know" the same as wrong answers. o1/o3/o4-mini rates (16%/33%/48%) match their PersonQA system card.

Minor misleading elements: 
- "Will always make things up... Always" overstates; paper shows positive but not 100% rate per response. 
- "Nearly half of what their most recent model tells you" exaggerates; 48% is specific to one fact-recall benchmark. 
- "9 out of 10" biggest benchmarks exact count unsubstantiated (paper says "most evaluations"). 
- "This is permanent" slightly overstated; paper notes socio-technical mitigation via eval changes is possible, though usability hit. 

No quotes/paraphrases distort the source. Tsinghua/DeepMind papers align independently on root causes.
